The difference was no longer statistically significant after adjusting for gender, because males were overrepresented in the PD group. The authors described the results as nonconclusive but in agreement with earlier studies that suggested an increased risk of skin cancer in PD.
quotes: Thirty-five PD patients (23.3%) presented skin lesions that could be classified as neoplastic or preneoplastic vs. 20 subjects in the control group (13.7%) (OR 95%, CI 1.92 [1.05, 3.51]).
However, this difference lost statistical significance when adjusted for gender (recruitment of controls was matched just for age with an over representation of males in the PD group).
Although nonconclusive, our results are in agreement with previous studies suggesting an increased risk of skin cancer in PD patients.

notes.statement: Ferreira et al. (2007) recommended that future epidemiological studies screen PD patients for actinic keratosis, citing how often it occurs in PD and its associated risk of melanoma.
quotes: The frequency of actinic keratosis in PD patients and the associated risk to develop melanoma recommends its screening in future epidemiological studies.

notes.statement: Constantinescu et al. (2007) found 5 cases of malignant melanoma in the DATATOP clinical trial cohort of patients with early Parkinson disease. Published values for a standard healthy population predicted 1.5 cases. The standardized event ratio was 3.3 (95% CI, 1.1-7.8), meaning melanoma incidence was higher than expected.
quotes: We identified all known cases of malignant melanoma (N = 5) in the DATATOP clinical trial cohort and compared that to published expected values (N = 1.5) for a standard healthy population.
The standardized event ratio was 3.3 (95% confidence interval, 1.1-7.8), indicating that incidence of malignant melanoma was higher than expected.

notes.statement: Constantinescu et al. (2007) found no association between levodopa therapy and the incidence of melanoma in patients with early Parkinson disease in the DATATOP cohort.
quotes: We found no association between levodopa therapy and the incidence of melanoma.

notes.statement: In a case-control study, Voon et al. (2007) compared 21 patients with idiopathic PD who developed pathological gambling after starting medication with 42 patients with PD who had no compulsive behaviors. Patients with pathological gambling had a younger age at PD onset and higher novelty seeking. They also more often had medication-induced hypomania or mania, impaired planning, or a personal or immediate family history of alcohol use disorders.
quotes: Patients with PG had a younger age at PD onset (P = .006), higher novelty seeking (P<.001), medication-induced hypomania or mania (P = .001), impaired planning (P = .002), or a personal or immediate family history of alcohol use disorders (P = .002).

notes.statement: Voon et al. (2007) found that novelty seeking, a personal or family history of alcohol use disorders, and younger age at PD onset together predicted pathological gambling with 83.7% accuracy. They concluded that patients with these features may have a greater risk of pathological gambling with dopamine agonists.
quotes: Novelty seeking, a personal or immediate family history of alcohol use disorders, and younger age at PD onset accurately predicted PG at 83.7% in a logistic regression model, with the model accounting for 62% of the variance.
Patients with PD having a younger age at PD onset, higher novelty seeking traits, and a personal or family history of alcohol use disorders may have a greater risk for PG with dopamine agonists.

notes.statement: Kreitzer and Malenka (2007) found that indirect-pathway striatal medium spiny neurons selectively expressed endocannabinoid-mediated long-term depression (eCB-LTD), which required dopamine D2 receptor activation. In models of Parkinson disease, indirect-pathway eCB-LTD was absent but was rescued by a D2 receptor agonist or by inhibitors of endocannabinoid degradation. Giving these drugs together in vivo reduced parkinsonian motor deficits.
quotes: indirect-pathway MSNs selectively express endocannabinoid-mediated long-term depression (eCB-LTD), which requires dopamine D2 receptor activation
In models of Parkinson's disease, indirect-pathway eCB-LTD is absent but is rescued by a D2 receptor agonist or inhibitors of endocannabinoid degradation.

Administration of these drugs together in vivo reduces parkinsonian motor deficits, suggesting that endocannabinoid-mediated depression of indirect-pathway synapses has a critical role in the control of movement.

notes.statement: Sotnikova et al. (2006) developed an acute model of severe dopamine deficiency using dopamine transporter knockout (DAT-KO) mice, in which striatal dopamine depends entirely on de novo synthesis; acute pharmacologic inhibition of tyrosine hydroxylase eliminated brain dopamine transiently (up to 16 hours). These dopamine-deficient DAT-KO (DDD) mice showed severe akinesia, rigidity, tremor, and ptosis, and the authors proposed them as a model for identifying compounds, including those acting independently of dopamine, for the treatment of Parkinson disease.
quotes: In the absence of a DAT-mediated recycling mechanism in these mice, striatal DA concentrations become entirely dependent on its de novo synthesis, and acute pharmacologic inhibition of tyrosine hydroxylase induces transient (up to 16 hours) elimination of brain DA.
Dopamine-deficient DAT-KO mice (DDD mice) demonstrate a striking behavioral phenotype manifested as severe akinesia, rigidity, tremor, and ptosis.
This model is particularly promising as a tool for evaluating the efficacy of compounds that may induce movement independently of DA.

notes.statement: Cooper et al. (2006) found that the earliest defect after alpha-synuclein expression in yeast was a block in endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-to-Golgi vesicular trafficking. In a genomewide screen, the largest class of toxicity modifiers were proteins acting at this step, including the Rab GTPase Ypt1p, which associated with cytoplasmic alpha-synuclein inclusions.
quotes: The earliest defect following alphaSyn expression in yeast was a block in endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-to-Golgi vesicular trafficking.

In a genomewide screen, the largest class of toxicity modifiers were proteins functioning at this same step, including the Rab guanosine triphosphatase Ypt1p, which associated with cytoplasmic alphaSyn inclusions.

notes.statement: Cooper et al. (2006) showed that elevated expression of Rab1, the mammalian homolog of YPT1, protected against alpha-synuclein-induced dopaminergic neuron loss in animal models of PD. They suggested that synucleinopathies may result from disruptions in basic cellular functions that interact with the unique biology of particular neurons to make them especially vulnerable.
quotes: Elevated expression of Rab1, the mammalian YPT1 homolog, protected against alphaSyn-induced dopaminergic neuron loss in animal models of PD.
Thus, synucleinopathies may result from disruptions in basic cellular functions that interface with the unique biology of particular neurons to make them especially vulnerable.

notes.statement: Zhang et al. (2006) reviewed early descriptions of Parkinson disease in ancient China.
quotes: Early descriptions of Parkinson disease in ancient China.

notes.statement: In a review, Muqit et al. (2006) stated that impaired mitochondrial function is thought to play a major role in the pathogenesis of Parkinson disease. They added that recent genetic advances suggest mitochondrial dysfunction may be the primary defect.
quotes: Impairment in mitochondrial dysfunction is thought to play a major role in the pathogenesis.
Recent genetic advances suggest that mitochondrial dysfunction may be the primary defect.

notes.statement: Muqit et al. (2006) suggested that drugs targeting the mitochondria may be the best hope for disease-modifying therapies in Parkinson disease.
quotes: Drugs that target the mitochondria may therefore represent the best hope for disease-modifying therapies in Parkinson disease.

notes.statement: Botella-López et al. (2006) found that the 180-kDa Reelin band was increased in the cerebrospinal fluid of patients with several neurodegenerative disorders, including Parkinson disease, frontotemporal dementia, progressive supranuclear palsy, and Alzheimer disease. In CSF, levels of the 180-kDa Reelin band correlated positively with Tau protein.
quotes: Next, we examined whether CSF Reelin levels were also altered in neurological diseases, including frontotemporal dementia, progressive supranuclear palsy, and Parkinson's disease. The Reelin 180-kDa band increased in all of the neurodegenerative disorders analyzed.
Moreover, the 180-kDa Reelin levels correlated positively with Tau protein in CSF.

notes.statement: Toft et al. (2006) screened 311 Norwegian patients with Parkinson disease and 474 controls for the GBA mutations N370S and L444P. A mutant GBA allele was found in 7 patients (2.3%) and 8 controls (1.7%) (p = 0.58). The authors concluded that the study did not indicate increased susceptibility to PD in GBA mutation carriers in Norway.
quotes: The authors screened a series of 311 Norwegian patients with PD and 474 controls for 2 common functional mutations of the GBA protein, N370S and L444P.
Seven patients (2.3%) and 8 controls (1.7%) carried a mutant GBA allele (p = 0.58).
This study does not indicate increased susceptibility to PD in GBA mutations carriers in Norway.

notes.statement: Fujita et al. (2006) imaged nicotinic acetylcholine receptors with SPECT and the ligand [123I]5-iodo-A-85380. They compared 10 nondemented Parkinson disease patients with 15 age-matched healthy controls. The patients showed a widespread, significant decrease of about 10% in total distribution volume in both cortical and subcortical regions, with no significant change in delivery (K1). The authors concluded that the study should be extended to demented patients.
quotes: Nicotinic acetylcholine receptors were imaged in 10 nondemented Parkinson's disease patients and 15 age-matched healthy subjects
Parkinson's disease showed a widespread significant decrease (approximately 10%) of V in both cortical and subcortical regions without a significant change in K(1).
These results indicate the importance of extending the study to demented patients.

notes.statement: Kwok et al. (2005) identified 2 functional SNPs in the GSK3B gene. The T allele of a promoter SNP (rs334558) had greater transcriptional activity in vitro. The T allele of an intronic SNP (rs6438552), which regulated splice acceptor site selection in vitro, was associated with altered splicing in lymphocytes and increased levels of GSK3B transcripts lacking exons 9 and 11, which correlated with enhanced Tau phosphorylation.
quotes: A promoter single nucleotide polymorphism (rs334558) is associated with transcriptional strength in vitro in which the T allele has greater activity.

The T allele is associated with altered splicing in lymphocytes and increased levels of GSK3B transcripts that lack exons 9 and 11 (GSKDeltaexon9+11). Increased levels of GSKDeltaexon9+11 correlated with enhanced phosphorylation of its substrate, Tau.

notes.statement: Kwok et al. (2005) found an increased frequency of the rs6438552 T allele in PD brains compared with control brains, with a corresponding increase in GSK3B exon 9+11-skipped transcripts and Tau phosphorylation. Conditional logistic regression indicated gene-gene interaction between the rs334558 T/T genotype and the MAPT H1/H1 haplotype (p = 0.009).
quotes: In a comparison of PD and control brains, there was increased in frequency of T allele (rs6438552) and corresponding increase in GSKDeltaexon9+11 and Tau phosphorylation in PD brains.
Conditional logistic regression indicated gene-gene interaction between T/T genotype of rs334558 and H1/H1 haplotype of microtubule-associated protein Tau (MAPT) gene (p = 0.009).

notes.statement: Kwok et al. (2005) found that a GSK3B haplotype carrying the T alleles of both polymorphisms was associated with PD risk after stratification by MAPT haplotype: odds ratio 1.64 (p = 0.007) in H1/H2 plus H2/H2 individuals and 0.68 (p less than 0.001) in H1/H1 individuals. They suggested that GSK3B polymorphisms interact with Tau haplotypes to modify PD risk.
quotes: There was association between a haplotype (T alleles of both GSK3B polymorphisms) and disease risk after stratification by Tau haplotypes ((H1/H2+H2/H2 individuals: odds ratio, 1.64; p = 0.007; (H1/H1 individuals: odds ratio, 0.68; p < 0.001).
Ours results suggest GSK3B polymorphisms alter transcription and splicing and interact with Tau haplotypes to modify disease risk in PD.

notes.statement: In a 2-tiered whole-genome association study of Parkinson disease, Maraganore et al. (2005) genotyped 198,345 SNPs in 443 sib pairs discordant for PD. They then tested 1,793 SNPs that were associated with PD in tier 1 in 332 matched case-unrelated control pairs. They identified 11 SNPs that were associated with PD (P less than 0.01) in both tiers and had the same direction of effect.
quotes: For tier 1, we individually genotyped 198,345 uniformly spaced and informative single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in 443 sibling pairs discordant for PD.
We identified 11 SNPs that were associated with PD (P<.01) in both tier 1 and tier 2 samples and had the same direction of effect.

notes.statement: Maraganore et al. (2005) found that a SNP within the SEMA5A gene had the lowest combined P value (P = 7.62 x 10(-6)). A second SNP tagged the PARK11 late-onset PD susceptibility locus (P = 1.70 x 10(-5)).
quotes: A SNP within the semaphorin 5A gene (SEMA5A) had the lowest combined P value (P=7.62 x 10(-6)).
A second SNP tagged the PARK11 late-onset PD susceptibility locus (P=1.70 x 10(-5)).

notes.statement: Maraganore et al. (2005) also genotyped 941 SNPs that were borderline significant in tier 1 and that tested a priori hypotheses. In the combined analysis, the 2 SNPs with the lowest P values (P = 9.07 x 10(-6) and P = 2.96 x 10(-5)) tagged the PARK10 late-onset PD susceptibility locus. The authors noted that independent replication across populations was needed.
quotes: In analysis of the combined tier 1 and tier 2b data, the two SNPs with the lowest P values (P=9.07 x 10(-6); P=2.96 x 10(-5)) tagged the PARK10 late-onset PD susceptibility locus.
Independent replication across populations will clarify the role of the genomic loci tagged by these SNPs in conferring PD susceptibility.

notes.statement: Maraganore et al. (2005) noted that the protein encoded by SEMA5A plays an important role in neurogenesis and in neuronal apoptosis, which they considered consistent with existing hypotheses about PD pathogenesis.
quotes: The protein encoded by this gene plays an important role in neurogenesis and in neuronal apoptosis, which is consistent with existing hypotheses regarding PD pathogenesis.

notes.statement: In a study of 276 outpatients with Parkinson disease, Paleacu et al. (2005) found hallucinations in 32% of patients. On stepwise logistic regression, risk factors for hallucinations were lower Mini-Mental State Examination score (p < 0.0001) and a positive family history of dementia (p = 0.0005).
quotes: Hallucinations were present in 32% of the 276 patients. Risk factors for hallucinations included Mini-Mental State Examination score (p < 0.0001) and positive family history of dementia (p = 0.0005).
Family history of dementia and lower Mini-Mental State Examination scores are risk factors for hallucinations in Parkinson disease.

notes.statement: Stien (2005) wrote about how parkinsonism is portrayed in the works of Shakespeare.
quotes: Shakespeare on parkinsonism.

notes.statement: Aharon-Peretz et al. (2004) screened 99 Ashkenazi Jewish patients with idiopathic Parkinson disease for 6 common GBA mutations and found that 31 (31.3%) carried 1 or 2 mutant alleles, compared with 4.1% of 74 Ashkenazi patients with Alzheimer disease and 6.2% of 1,543 healthy Ashkenazi controls. Patients with PD had significantly greater odds of being Gaucher disease carriers than patients with Alzheimer disease (odds ratio, 10.8) or controls (odds ratio, 7.0). The authors suggested that heterozygosity for a GBA mutation may predispose Ashkenazi Jews to Parkinson disease.
quotes: Thirty-one patients with Parkinson's disease (31.3 percent; 95 percent confidence interval, 22.2 to 40.4 percent) had one or two mutant GBA alleles

Patients with Parkinson's disease had significantly greater odds of being carriers of Gaucher's disease than did patients with Alzheimer's disease (odds ratio, 10.8; 95 percent confidence interval, 3.0 to 46.6; P<0.001) or control subjects (odds ratio, 7.0; 95 percent confidence interval, 4.2 to 11.4; P<0.001).
Our results suggest that heterozygosity for a GBA mutation may predispose Ashkenazi Jews to Parkinson's disease.

notes.statement: Aharon-Peretz et al. (2004) found that among Ashkenazi patients with Parkinson disease, carriers of GBA mutations had an earlier age at onset than noncarriers (mean, 60.0 vs 64.2 years; P = 0.04).
quotes: Among the patients with Parkinson's disease, patients who were carriers of Gaucher's disease were younger than those who were not carriers (mean [+/-SD] age at onset, 60.0+/-14.2 years vs. 64.2+/-11.7 years; P=0.04).

notes.statement: Aharon-Peretz et al. (2004) identified 95 Gaucher disease carriers (6.2%) among 1,543 healthy Ashkenazi Jews: 92 were heterozygous for N370S and 3 for 84GG.
quotes: Ninety-five carriers of Gaucher's disease were identified among the 1543 control subjects (6.2 percent; 95 percent confidence interval, 5.0 to 7.4 percent): 92 were heterozygous for N370S, and 3 were heterozygous for 84GG.

notes.statement: Wirdefeldt et al. (2004) screened 33,780 twins in 14,082 pairs from the Swedish Twin Registry for PD by telephone interview and by linkage to the Swedish Inpatient Discharge Register. They identified 247 twins with possible PD. Only 2 pairs were concordant for possible PD, and both were female dizygotic pairs. Concordance stayed low in all zygosity groups when twins with suspected parkinsonism or another movement disorder were also counted as affected.
quotes: The authors screened 33,780 twins in 14,082 pairs for PD by telephone interviews and linked the STR to the Swedish Inpatient Discharge Register.

For possible PD, there were only two concordant pairs, both female dizygotic. Similarly, concordances were low in all zygosity groups when the definition of affected was expanded to include twins with suspected parkinsonism or movement disorder in addition to possible PD.

notes.statement: Wirdefeldt et al. (2004) found that the best-fitting structural equation model contained only environmental components of variance. The familial component appeared marginally larger in women. They concluded that environmental factors are most important in the etiology of PD and that the importance of genetic effects is notably low compared with other complex diseases.
quotes: Sex differences in the relative importance of genetic and environmental effects were indicated with a marginally larger familial component in women. The best-fitting structural equation model included only environmental components of variance.
These results suggest that environmental factors are most important in the etiology of PD. Compared with other complex diseases, the importance of genetic effects in PD is notably low.

notes.statement: In a 3-phase community-based door-to-door survey in central Singapore of people aged 50 years and older (participation 67% of 22,279 eligible), Tan et al. (2004) identified 46 people with PD, 16 of them newly diagnosed. Age-adjusted to the 1970 US census, the prevalence was 0.30% (95% CI, 0.22-0.41), and it rose significantly with age.
quotes: The participation rate was 67% among 22,279 eligible individuals. Forty-six participants with PD were identified of which 16 were newly diagnosed cases.
The prevalence rate of PD for those aged 50 and above in Singapore was 0.30% (95% CI: 0.22 to 0.41), age-adjusted to US 1970 census. The prevalence rates increased significantly with age.

notes.statement: Tan et al. (2004) found the same age-adjusted PD prevalence in Singaporean Chinese (0.33%), Malays (0.29%) and Indians (0.28%) (p = 1.0). The rates were comparable to those in Western countries. The authors concluded that environmental factors may matter more than racially determined genetic factors in the development of PD.
quotes: The age-adjusted prevalence rates among Chinese (0.33%, 95% CI: 0.22 to 0.48), Malays (0.29%, 95% CI: 0.13 to 0.67), and Indians (0.28%, 95% CI: 0.12 to 0.67) were the same (p = 1.0).
Environmental factors may be more important than racially determined genetic factors in the development of PD.

notes.statement: Li et al. (2003) noted that they had previously reported linkage of loci controlling age at onset in Alzheimer disease and Parkinson disease to a 15-cM region on chromosome 10q.
quotes: We previously reported genetic linkage of loci controlling age-at-onset in Alzheimer disease (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD) to a 15 cM region on chromosome 10q.

notes.statement: Li et al. (2003) used 'genomic convergence' to choose candidate genes. They combined the 10q linkage region with hippocampal expression differences between Alzheimer disease patients and controls. Allelic association studies used 1,362 samples from their Parkinson disease dataset (635 patients) and 2,814 samples from their Alzheimer disease dataset. They found significant age-at-onset associations for GSTO1 (P = 0.007) and for the neighbouring gene GSTO2 (P = 0.005), but none for SCD, NDUFB8, or PRSS11.
quotes: Using 2814 samples from our AD dataset (1773 AD patients) and 1362 samples from our PD dataset (635 PD patients), allelic association studies for age-at-onset effects in AD and PD revealed no association for three of the candidates
but a significant association was found for GSTO1 (P=0.007) and a second transcribed member of the GST omega class, GSTO2 (P=0.005), located next to GSTO1.

notes.statement: Li et al. (2003) noted that GSTO1 may be involved in the post-translational modification of interleukin-1-beta. They described this as provocative because inflammation may play a role in Parkinson and Alzheimer disease.
quotes: recent data suggest that GSTO1 maybe involved in the post-translational modification of the inflammatory cytokine interleukin-1beta. This is provocative given reports of the possible role of inflammation in these two neurodegenerative disorders.

notes.statement: Marder et al. (2003) compared first-degree relatives of 221 PD probands with onset at age 50 or younger and 266 probands with onset after age 50 against relatives of 409 control probands. The risk of PD was similarly raised in relatives of early-onset probands (RR 2.9) and of late-onset probands (RR 2.7).
quotes: We estimated the degree of increased risk of PD in first-degree relatives of 221 PD probands with age of onset 50 years or younger and 266 PD probands with age of onset older than 50 years compared with the first-degree relatives of 409 control probands.

Risk of PD was similar among first-degree relatives of early-onset PD probands (risk ratio [RR], 2.9; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.6-5.0; p = 0.0002) and late-onset PD probands (RR, 2.7; 95% CI, 1.6-4.4; p = 0.0002)

notes.statement: In late-onset families, Marder et al. (2003) found that both siblings (RR 3.6) and parents (RR 2.5) had a higher risk of PD than control relatives. In early-onset families, only siblings had a markedly higher risk (RR 7.9) and parents did not. The authors concluded that this pattern was consistent with an autosomal recessive contribution to early-onset but not late-onset PD, and that the specific genes and mode of inheritance may differ between the two groups.
quotes: In late-onset families, both siblings (RR, 3.6; 95% CI, 1.3-10.3; p = 0.02) and parents (RR, 2.5; 95% CI, 1.4-4.6; p = 0.003) were at increased risk compared with control relatives.
This pattern is consistent with an autosomal recessive contribution to the inheritance of early but not late-onset PD.
Genetic factors are important in both early- and late-onset PD, but specific genes and mode of inheritance may differ between the two groups.

notes.statement: SPELLMAN (1962) reported familial cases of parkinsonism and presented evidence of a dominant trait in one patient's family.
quotes: Report of familial cases of parkinsonism. Evidence of a dominant trait in a patient's family.

notes.statement: Pankratz et al. (2003) carried out a genome-wide nonparametric linkage analysis in 754 affected individuals (425 sib pairs) from 362 multiplex PD families. In the 216 sib pairs with verified PD, the maximum lod score was 3.4 on chromosome 2. When all 425 affected sib pairs were included, the lod score was 3.1 on the X chromosome.
quotes: Model I included only those individuals with a more stringent diagnosis of verified PD (216 sibling pairs) and resulted in a maximum LOD score of 3.4 on chromosome 2.
Model II included all affected individuals (425 sibling pairs) and yielded a LOD score of 3.1 on the X chromosome.

notes.statement: Pankratz et al. (2003) analyzed subsets of families. In the 85 families with a very strong family history of PD, they found linkage to chromosome 2 (lod = 4.9) and a lod score of 2.4 on chromosome 14. In the 277 families without a strong family history, they found linkage to chromosome 10 (lod = 2.4) and the X chromosome (lod = 3.2).
quotes: The 85 families with a very strong family history of PD were employed in a genome screen and, in addition to strong evidence of linkage to chromosome 2 (LOD=4.9), also produced a LOD of 2.4 on chromosome 14.
A genome screen performed in the 277 families without a strong family history of PD detected linkage to chromosomes 10 (LOD=2.4) and X (LOD=3.2).

notes.statement: Pankratz et al. (2003) ran a genome screen in 23 families in which PD patients had a mutation in only one allele of the parkin gene and found evidence of linkage to chromosome 10 (lod = 2.3). They concluded that their findings supported the hypothesis that gene-by-gene (epistatic) interactions are important in PD susceptibility.
quotes: A genome screen using the 23 families with PD patients having a mutation in only one allele of the parkin gene detected evidence of linkage to chromosome 10 (LOD=2.3).
These findings demonstrate consistent evidence of linkage to chromosomes 2 and X and also support the hypothesis that gene-by-gene interactions are important in PD susceptibility.

notes.statement: Scherzer et al. (2003) profiled genome-wide expression in transgenic Drosophila expressing human alpha-synuclein at presymptomatic, early, and advanced disease stages and identified 51 signature transcripts, including lipid, energy, and membrane transport mRNAs, tightly associated with alpha-synuclein expression. Expression changes revealed specific pathology already at the presymptomatic stage, whereas these alpha-synuclein-associated genes were transcribed normally in age-matched tau transgenic flies, suggesting highly distinct pathways of neurodegeneration.
quotes: Fifty-one signature transcripts, including lipid, energy and membrane transport mRNAs, were tightly associated with alpha-synuclein expression.
at the pre-symptomatic stage, when the potential for neuroprotection is greatest, expression changes revealed specific pathology
In age-matched tau transgenic Drosophila, the transcription of alpha-synuclein associated genes was normal, suggesting highly distinct pathways of neurodegeneration.

notes.statement: Bembi et al. (2003) noted that the parkinsonism previously reported with type 1 Gaucher disease was characterized mainly by bilateral akinetic-rigid signs and a poor response to levodopa. In contrast, their 4 patients showed typical PD, with asymmetric onset and a good response to treatment.
quotes: The clinical picture is characterized by the predominance of bilateral akinetic-rigid signs and poor response to levodopa therapy.

notes.statement: Marx et al. (2003) screened the synphilin-1 gene in 328 German patients with familial or sporadic PD. They found a novel R621C mutation in 2 apparently sporadic patients. The mutation was not present in 702 chromosomes from healthy German controls.
quotes: we performed a detailed mutation analysis of the synphilin-1 gene in 328 German familial and sporadic PD patients
This mutation was absent in a total of 702 chromosomes of healthy German controls.

notes.statement: In SH-SY5Y cells, Marx et al. (2003) found that synphilin-1 formed cytoplasmic inclusions. Under proteasomal inhibition, cells expressing C621 synphilin-1 formed significantly fewer inclusions than cells expressing wildtype protein. The mutant-expressing cells were also more susceptible to staurosporine-induced cell death. The authors suggested that inclusion formation may be beneficial to cells and that a mutation reducing this ability may sensitize neurons to cellular stress.
quotes: we observed a significantly reduced number of inclusions in cells expressing C621 synphilin-1 compared with cells expressing wild-type (wt) synphilin-1, when subjected to proteasomal inhibition
C621 synphilin-1 transfected cells were more susceptible to staurosporine-induced cell death than cells expressing wt synphilin-1.
suggest that the formation of intracellular inclusions may be beneficial to cells and that a mutation in synphilin-1 that reduces this ability may sensitize neurons to cellular stress

notes.statement: Teismann et al. (2003) found that COX-2, the rate-limiting enzyme in prostaglandin E2 synthesis, was upregulated in brain dopaminergic neurons of both PD patients and MPTP-treated mice. After MPTP administration, COX-2 was induced through a JNK/c-Jun-dependent mechanism.
quotes: Here we show that COX-2, the rate-limiting enzyme in prostaglandin E(2) synthesis, is up-regulated in brain dopaminergic neurons of both PD and MPTP mice.
COX-2 induction occurs through a JNKc-Jun-dependent mechanism after MPTP administration.

notes.statement: In MPTP mice, Teismann et al. (2003) showed that targeting COX-2 did not protect against dopaminergic neurodegeneration by reducing inflammation. Instead, COX-2 inhibition prevented formation of the oxidant species dopamine-quinone. The authors suggested that COX-2 plays a critical role in both the pathogenesis and the selectivity of PD neurodegeneration.
quotes: We demonstrate that targeting COX-2 does not protect against MPTP-induced dopaminergic neurodegeneration by mitigating inflammation.
Instead, we provide evidence that COX-2 inhibition prevents the formation of the oxidant species dopamine-quinone, which has been implicated in the pathogenesis of PD.

notes.statement: Teismann et al. (2003) suggested that COX-2 inhibitors may be therapies for PD, because of their safety record and their ability to penetrate the blood-brain barrier.
quotes: Because of the safety record of the COX-2 inhibitors, and their ability to penetrate the blood-brain barrier, these drugs may be therapies for PD.

notes.statement: In a phase 1 safety trial, Gill et al. (2003) infused GDNF directly into the putamen of 5 patients with Parkinson disease. After 1 year there were no serious clinical side effects. The off-medication UPDRS motor subscore improved by 39%, and the activities of daily living subscore improved by 61%. Medication-induced dyskinesias fell by 64% and were not seen off medication.
quotes: Here we delivered GDNF directly into the putamen of five Parkinson patients in a phase 1 safety trial.

After one year, there were no serious clinical side effects, a 39% improvement in the off-medication motor sub-score of the Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale (UPDRS) and a 61% improvement in the activities of daily living sub-score.
Medication-induced dyskinesias were reduced by 64% and were not observed off medication during chronic GDNF delivery.

notes.statement: Gill et al. (2003) found that [18F]dopamine PET showed a significant 28% increase in putamen dopamine storage after 18 months of GDNF infusion. They suggested this reflected a direct effect of GDNF on dopamine function. One catheter had to be repositioned, and MRI changes resolved after the GDNF concentration was lowered.
quotes: Positron emission tomography (PET) scans of [(18)F]dopamine uptake showed a significant 28% increase in putamen dopamine storage after 18 months, suggesting a direct effect of GDNF on dopamine function.
One catheter needed to be repositioned and there were changes in the magnetic resonance images that disappeared after lowering the concentration of GDNF.

notes.statement: In a review, Warner and Schapira (2003) concluded that most cases of Parkinson disease are likely caused by a complex interplay between genetic and environmental factors. They cited evidence from twin and family studies, from the mapping and cloning of PARK genes, and from analysis of potential susceptibility genes.
quotes: It is likely that for most cases, there is a complex interplay between these genetic and environmental influences in the causation of Parkinson's disease.
This has come from twin and family studies, the mapping and cloning of PARK genes that are associated with the development of PD, and analysis of potential susceptibility genes.

notes.statement: In a study of 99 Chinese patients with PD and 126 controls from Hong Kong, Chan et al. (2003) used PCR-RFLP to type the M1, M2, and M3 NAT2 polymorphisms. The NAT2 slow acetylator genotype was significantly more frequent in patients than in controls (68.7% vs 28.6%), with an odds ratio of 5.53 (95% CI 3.08 to 9.92) after adjusting for age, sex, and smoking history.
quotes: The authors obtained DNA samples and documented sex, age, and smoking history in 99 Chinese patients with PD and in 126 control subjects from two major Hong Kong hospitals.

The frequency of the slow acetylator genotype for N-acetyltransferase 2 in the PD group was significantly higher than that of the control group (68.7% vs 28.6%) with an OR of 5.53 (95% CI 3.08 to 9.92) after adjusting for age, sex, and smoking history.

notes.statement: Chan et al. (2003) found in a subgroup analysis that smoking had no modifying effect on the association between NAT2 genotype and PD. They suggested that the finding provides evidence for a possible functional relationship between the NAT2 slow acetylator genotype and PD in both Chinese and white subjects.
quotes: In a subgroup analysis smoking had no modifying effect on the association between genotype and PD.
provides evidence for a possible functional relationship between NAT2 slow acetylator genotype and PD in both racial groups.

notes.statement: van der Walt et al. (2003) genotyped 10 SNPs defining European mtDNA haplogroups in 609 white patients with PD and 340 unaffected white controls. Compared with carriers of the most common haplogroup, H, individuals with haplogroup J (OR 0.55; P = 0.02) or K (OR 0.52; P = 0.02) had a significantly decreased risk of PD.
quotes: we genotyped 10 single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) that define the European mtDNA haplogroups in 609 white patients with PD and 340 unaffected white control subjects

individuals classified as haplogroup J (odds ratio [OR] 0.55; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.34-0.91; P=.02) or K (OR 0.52; 95% CI 0.30-0.90; P=.02) demonstrated a significant decrease in risk of PD versus individuals carrying the most common haplogroup, H

notes.statement: van der Walt et al. (2003) found that SNP 10398G, which defines haplogroups J and K and causes a nonconservative thr-to-ala change in the ND3 subunit of complex I, was strongly associated with protection against PD (OR 0.53; P = 0.0001). The protective effect seemed stronger in women (OR 0.43; P = 0.0009). The authors suggested that ND3 is an important factor in PD susceptibility among white individuals.
quotes: a specific SNP that defines these two haplogroups, 10398G, is strongly associated with this protective effect (OR 0.53; 95% CI 0.39-0.73; P=.0001)
SNP 10398G causes a nonconservative amino acid change from threonine to alanine within the NADH dehydrogenase 3 (ND3) of complex I
After stratification by sex, this decrease in risk appeared stronger in women than in men (OR 0.43; 95% CI 0.27-0.71; P=.0009)

notes.statement: van der Walt et al. (2003) found that SNP 9055A in the ATP6 gene had a protective effect against PD in women (OR 0.45; P = 0.03).
quotes: In addition, SNP 9055A of ATP6 demonstrated a protective effect for women (OR 0.45; 95% CI 0.22-0.93; P=.03).

notes.statement: Várkonyi et al. (2003) found no mutations in the parkin or alpha-synuclein genes in 4 patients who had both Gaucher disease and parkinsonism. They suggested that the co-occurrence of the two phenotypes points to a shared pathway, a modifier, or another genetic cause.
quotes: No mutations were identified in the genes for parkin or alpha-synuclein.
The concurrence of these two phenotypes, both in this series of patients and in others in the literature, suggests a shared pathway, modifier, or other genetic etiology.

notes.statement: In a community-based case-control study of 209 Parkinson disease patients and 488 matched controls of European (mostly French) ancestry enrolled in a French agricultural health insurance organization, Levecque et al. (2003) found association of PD with a polymorphism in exon 29 of nNOS (NOS1) (OR for T allele carriers = 1.53, P = 0.02) and a protective association with a polymorphism in exon 22 of iNOS (NOS2) (OR for AA carriers = 0.50, P = 0.01); a polymorphism in exon 18 of nNOS showed no association (OR = 1.20, P = 0.30).
quotes: Two-hundred and nine PD patients and 488 controls of European (mostly French) ancestry and matched for age, sex and region of residency were included in this study.

Associations were observed with polymorphisms present in exon 22 of iNOS (OR for AA carriers=0.50, 95% CI=0.29-0.86, P=0.01) and in exon 29 of nNOS (OR for carriers of the T allele=1.53, 95% CI=1.08-2.16, P=0.02)
no association was observed with a polymorphism in exon 18 of nNOS (OR for carriers of the T allele=1.20, 95% CI=0.85-1.69, P=0.30)

notes.statement: Levecque et al. (2003) found a significant interaction of the nNOS polymorphisms with current and ever cigarette smoking (nNOS exon 18, P = 0.05; nNOS exon 29, P = 0.04), and concluded that the data favored an involvement of nNOS and iNOS as modifier genes in PD.
quotes: Moreover, a significant interaction of the nNOS polymorphisms with current and ever cigarette smoking was found (nNOS 18, P=0.05; nNOS 29, P=0.04).
All together, these data favour an involvement of these two genes as new modifier genes in PD.

notes.statement: Mattila et al. (2002) reported an association between Parkinson disease and a polymorphism at position -511 of the interleukin-1-beta gene (IL1B) in Finnish patients.
quotes: Association of an interleukin 1B gene polymorphism (-511) with Parkinson's disease in Finnish patients.

notes.statement: Pankratz et al. (2002) performed a genome screen with multipoint nonparametric linkage analysis in 160 multiplex PD families without parkin mutations. In the 96 sibling pairs (90 families) with verified PD (model I), the highest LOD scores were on chromosome X (LOD 2.1) and chromosome 2 (LOD 1.9). When all examined individuals were counted as affected (170 sibling pairs, model II), the scores rose to 2.7 for chromosome X and 2.5 for chromosome 2.
quotes: Under model I, the highest LOD scores were observed on chromosome X (LOD score 2.1) and on chromosome 2 (LOD score 1.9).
Analyses performed with all available sibling pairs (model II) found even greater evidence of linkage to chromosome X (LOD score 2.7) and to chromosome 2 (LOD score 2.5).

notes.statement: Pankratz et al. (2002) also found evidence of linkage to chromosomes 4, 5, and 13 (LOD scores greater than 1.5). They noted that their findings agreed with other linkage studies that had reported linkage to chromosomes 5 and X.
quotes: Evidence of linkage was also found to chromosomes 4, 5, and 13 (LOD scores >1.5).
Our findings are consistent with those of other linkage studies that have reported linkage to chromosomes 5 and X.

notes.statement: Among 203 PD sibling pairs, Pankratz et al. (2002) found parkin mutations in 22 families. To reduce genetic heterogeneity, they left these families out of the genome screen.
quotes: Families with positive LOD scores for a marker in an intron of the parkin gene were prioritized for parkin-gene testing, and mutations in the parkin gene were identified in 22 families.
To reduce genetic heterogeneity, these families were not included in subsequent genome-screen analysis.

notes.statement: Maher et al. (2002) performed a segregation analysis on the nuclear families of 948 consecutively ascertained PD index cases from 3 US centers. Affected fathers were reported in 4.7%, mothers in 6.6%, brothers in 2.9%, and sisters in 3.2%. Most index cases were male, but slightly more of the reported affected relatives were female.
quotes: the proportion of affected fathers (4.7%), mothers (6.6%), brothers (2.9%), and sisters (3.2%) were similar across the three sites
While most of the index cases were male, modestly more of the reported affected relatives were female.

notes.statement: Maher et al. (2002) found support for a rare major Mendelian gene for PD in both an age-of-onset model and a susceptibility model. The age-of-onset model pointed to a gene that affects age-dependent penetrance by influencing age at onset rather than susceptibility. The authors could not tell whether the two analyses were modeling the same gene or different genes. They suggested that reduced penetrance through gene-environment interactions might explain the low concordance in monozygotic twins.
quotes: These analyses support the presence of a rare major Mendelian gene for PD in both the age-of-onset and susceptibility model.
The age-of-onset model provides evidence for a gene that influences age-dependent penetrance of PD, influencing age of onset rather than susceptibility.
Such gene environment interactions, involving reduced penetrance in PD, may explain the low concordance rates among monozygotic twins for this disease.

notes.statement: Li et al. (2002) carried out a genomic screen for age at onset in 174 Parkinson disease families. They found heritabilities of 40 to 60% and significant evidence of linkage of age at onset to chromosome 1p (lod = 3.41).
quotes: a genomic screen was performed for AAO in families with Alzheimer disease (AD; n=449) and Parkinson disease (PD; n=174). Heritabilities between 40%--60% were found in both the AD and PD data sets.
For PD, significant evidence for linkage to AAO was found on chromosome 1p (LOD = 3.41).

notes.statement: Li et al. (2002) found evidence of age-at-onset linkage on chromosomes 6 and 10 independently in both Alzheimer disease and PD families. A unified analysis found a single peak on 10q between D10S1239 and D10S1237 (maximum lod = 2.62), which suggested that a common gene affects age at onset in both diseases.
quotes: evidence for AAO linkage on chromosomes 6 and 10 was identified independently in both the AD and PD data sets.
Subsequent unified analyses of these regions identified a single peak on chromosome 10q between D10S1239 and D10S1237, with a maximum LOD score of 2.62.
These data suggest that a common gene affects AAO in these two common complex neurodegenerative diseases.

notes.statement: Racette et al. (2002) calculated a minimum prevalence of PD of 552 per 100,000 among persons 40 years and older in an Old-Order Amish community, higher than in the general population.
quotes: In the index Amish community, a minimum prevalence of PD in the population 40 years and older of 552/100,000 was calculated.

notes.statement: Racette et al. (2002) found that the mean kinship coefficient among Amish subjects with PD or PD by history (0.036) was higher than in age-matched normal Amish controls (0.016; p = 0.007), providing evidence that PD is inherited in this family.
quotes: The mean kinship coefficient in the subjects with PD and those with PD by history (0.036) was higher (p = 0.007) than in a group of age-matched normal Amish control subjects (0.016), providing evidence that PD is inherited in this family.

notes.statement: In a large Old-Order Amish PD kindred, Racette et al. (2002) found no mutations in known PD genes, and no haplotype cosegregated with disease in previously linked PD regions; they suggested that the increased prevalence may be due in part to a novel gene or genes.
quotes: Sequence analysis did not detect any mutations in known PD genes. No single haplotype cosegregates with the disease in any of the chromosomal regions previously found to be linked to PD, and no marker in these regions exhibits increased homozygosity among definite PD cases.
this increased prevalence may be due in part to a novel gene(s).

notes.statement: In Drosophila, Auluck et al. (2002) found that directed expression of the molecular chaperone Hsp70 prevented the dopaminergic neuronal loss associated with alpha-synuclein expression. Interfering with endogenous chaperone activity accelerated alpha-synuclein toxicity.
quotes: We report that directed expression of the molecular chaperone Hsp70 prevented dopaminergic neuronal loss associated with alpha-synuclein in Drosophila and that interference with endogenous chaperone activity accelerated alpha-synuclein toxicity.

notes.statement: Auluck et al. (2002) found that Lewy bodies in human postmortem tissue immunostained for molecular chaperones. They suggested that chaperones may play a role in the progression of Parkinson disease.
quotes: Lewy bodies in human postmortem tissue immunostained for molecular chaperones, also suggesting that chaperones may play a role in Parkinson's disease progression.

notes.statement: In 235 families with idiopathic PD (426 affected and 579 unaffected members), Martin et al. (2001) found significant family-based association with PD for 3 of 5 tau gene SNPs tested (SNP 3, P = 0.03; SNP 9i, P = 0.04; SNP 11, P = 0.04). Haplotype analysis gave stronger evidence, with positive association for one haplotype (P = 0.009) and negative association for another (P = 0.007).
quotes: Analysis of association between the SNPs and PD yielded significant evidence of association for 3 of the 5 SNPs tested: SNP 3, P =.03; SNP 9i, P =.04; and SNP 11, P =.04.
Strong evidence of association was found with haplotype analysis, with a positive association with one haplotype (P =.009) and a negative association with another haplotype (P =.007).

notes.statement: Martin et al. (2001) noted that they had previously observed linkage of idiopathic PD to chromosome 17q21, a region containing the tau gene. They concluded that combining linkage with positional association analysis implicated tau as a susceptibility gene for idiopathic PD.
quotes: We recently observed linkage in idiopathic Parkinson disease (PD) to a region on chromosome 17q21 that contains the tau gene.
This integrated approach of genetic linkage and positional association analyses implicates tau as a susceptibility gene for idiopathic PD.

notes.statement: Martin et al. (2001) found substantial linkage disequilibrium (P less than 0.001) among 4 of the 5 tau SNPs tested (SNPs 3, 9i, 9ii, and 11).
quotes: Substantial linkage disequilibrium (P<.001) was detected between 4 of the 5 SNPs (SNPs 3, 9i, 9ii, and 11).

notes.statement: Scott et al. (2001) performed a complete genomic screen with 344 markers in 174 families with multiple individuals with idiopathic PD and found significant evidence for linkage to chromosomes 17q (MLOD = 2.28; LOD = 2.62), 8p (MLOD = 2.01; LOD = 2.22), and 5q (MLOD = 2.39; LOD = 1.50) overall and in families with late-onset PD, and to chromosome 9q (MLOD = 1.52; LOD = 2.59) in families with both levodopa-responsive and levodopa-nonresponsive patients.
quotes: chromosomes 17q (MLOD = 2.28; LOD = 2.62), 8p (MLOD = 2.01; LOD = 2.22), and 5q (MLOD = 2.39; LOD = 1.50) overall and in families with late-onset PD, and chromosome 9q (MLOD = 1.52; LOD = 2.59) in families with both levodopa-responsive and levodopa-nonresponsive patients

notes.statement: Scott et al. (2001) found linkage to the parkin gene region on chromosome 6 (MLOD = 5.07; LOD = 5.47) in families with at least 1 individual with PD onset before age 40 years, and concluded that parkin is important in early-onset PD and that multiple genetic factors may be important in idiopathic late-onset PD.
quotes: chromosome 6 in the parkin gene (MLOD = 5.07; LOD = 5.47) in families with at least 1 individual with PD onset at younger than 40 years
Our data suggest that the parkin gene is important in early-onset PD and that multiple genetic factors may be important in the development of idiopathic late-onset PD.

notes.statement: Tayebi et al. (2001) reported that a pallidotomy at age 47 years was unsuccessful in a woman with Gaucher disease and parkinsonism. Her motor and cognitive decline continued despite enzyme replacement therapy.
quotes: A pallidotomy at age 47 was unsuccessful. Her motor and cognitive deterioration progressed despite enzyme replacement therapy.

notes.statement: Tayebi et al. (2001) suggested that gene changes linked to a new rearrangement could contribute to the atypical parkinsonian phenotype. The rearrangement arose from a crossover between the metaxin gene and its pseudogene.
quotes: Gene alterations associated with this novel rearrangement, resulting from a crossover between the gene for metaxin and its pseudogene, could contribute to the atypical phenotype encountered in this patient.

notes.statement: Vaughan et al. (2001) reviewed the genetics of parkinsonism and noted that 2 genes (SNCA and parkin) and 2 further loci had been implicated in familial PD. They also noted that UCHL1 mutations had been described in familial PD, although the evidence for a role of UCHL1 was less clear.
quotes: Two genes (SNCA and parkin) as well as two gene loci have now been implicated in the pathogenesis of familial PD.
Mutations in a further gene, UCHL1, have been described in familial PD although the evidence for its role in PD is less clear.

notes.statement: Vaughan et al. (2001) suggested that nigral degeneration with Lewy body formation, and the clinical picture of PD that results, may be a final common pathway of a multifactorial disease process involving both environmental and genetic factors. They cited low heritability in the general population, the rarity of large families, and genetic heterogeneity.
quotes: Nigral degeneration with Lewy body formation and the resulting clinical picture of PD may represent a final common pathway of a multifactorial disease process in which both environmental and genetic factors have a role.
considering the rarity of large families, low heritability in the general population and genetic heterogeneity

notes.statement: In a case-control study of 224 Taiwanese patients with PD and 197 matched controls, Wu et al. (2001) found that the MAOB intron 13 G genotype (G in men and G/G in women) was associated with a 2.07-fold increased relative risk of PD.
quotes: Two hundred twenty-four patients with PD and 197 controls, matched for age, sex, and birthplace, were recruited.
The MAOB G genotype (G in men and G:/G in women) was associated with a 2.07-fold increased relative risk of PD.

notes.statement: Wu et al. (2001) found that the COMT Val158Met polymorphism alone showed no correlation with PD risk in Taiwanese, but a significant synergistic enhancement of risk was found in patients carrying both the COMT L and MAOB G genotypes, suggesting an interaction of these two dopamine-metabolizing enzymes in the pathogenesis of sporadic PD. The authors cautioned that the low frequencies of the combined genotypes required confirmation in a larger sample.
quotes: COMT polymorphism, considered alone, showed no correlation with PD risk; however, a significant synergistic enhancement was found in PD patients harboring both the COMT(L) and MAOB G genotypes.

indicating an interaction of these two dopamine-metabolizing enzymes in the pathogenesis of sporadic PD. However, the relatively low frequencies of these combined genotypes in our study necessitates confirmation with a larger sample size.

notes.statement: Sveinbjörnsdottir et al. (2000) used a genealogic database covering 610,920 Icelanders over 11 centuries and found that 772 patients with Parkinson disease, including 560 with late-onset disease (onset after age 50 years), were significantly more related to each other than matched controls were, and that this relatedness reached beyond the nuclear family.
quotes: With the use of an extensive computerized data base containing genealogic information on 610,920 people in Iceland during the past 11 centuries

Patients with Parkinson's disease, including a subgroup of 560 patients with late-onset disease (onset at >50 years of age), were significantly more related to each other than were subjects in matched groups of controls, and this relatedness extended beyond the nuclear family.

notes.statement: In relatives of patients with late-onset Parkinson disease, Sveinbjörnsdottir et al. (2000) found a risk ratio of 6.7 for sibs, 3.2 for offspring and 2.7 for nephews and nieces. They concluded that late-onset Parkinson disease has both a genetic and an environmental component.
quotes: The risk ratio for Parkinson's disease was 6.7 (95 percent confidence interval, 4.3 to 9.6) for siblings, 3.2 (95 percent confidence interval, 1.2 to 7.8) for offspring, and 2.7 (95 percent confidence interval, 1.6 to 3.9) for nephews and nieces of patients with late-onset Parkinson's disease.
Late-onset Parkinson's disease has a genetic component as well as an environmental component.

notes.statement: Clarke et al. (2000) found that the kinetics of neuronal death in models of photoreceptor degeneration, in excitotoxic hippocampal cell death, in a mouse model of cerebellar degeneration, and in Parkinson and Huntington diseases were exponential. These kinetics were better explained by models in which the risk of cell death stays constant or decreases exponentially with age, which argued against the cumulative damage hypothesis. The authors proposed a 'one-hit' model in which mutation imposes a mutant steady state on the neuron and a single random event initiates cell death.
quotes: Here we show in contrast that the kinetics of neuronal death in 12 models of photoreceptor degeneration, hippocampal neurons undergoing excitotoxic cell death, a mouse model of cerebellar degeneration and Parkinson's and Huntington's diseases are all exponential
Our findings are most simply accommodated by a 'one-hit' biochemical model in which mutation imposes a mutant steady state on the neuron and a single event randomly initiates cell death.

notes.statement: Montgomery et al. (1999) applied a PD test battery covering motor function, olfaction, and mood to 80 asymptomatic first-degree relatives of PD patients and 100 normal controls. Abnormal scores occurred in 22.5% of relatives versus 9% of controls, a statistically significant difference. The authors suggested that the battery may detect the asymptomatic carrier state or risk for PD.
quotes: Eighty FDRs and 100 NC subjects were tested. Of the FDRs, 22.5% scored in the abnormal range, and 9% of NC subjects had abnormal scores. This difference was statistically significant.
Thus, the PD Battery may detect the asymptomatic carrier state or risk for PD.

notes.statement: Montgomery et al. (1999) found that among sons and daughters of PD patients who had abnormal scores on the PD test battery, the affected parent was much more often the father.
quotes: Among the sons and daughters whose scores were abnormal, there was a much higher prevalence of the affected parent being the father.
Sons and daughters whose scores were in the abnormal range were more likely to have fathers with PD.

notes.statement: In a study of 19,842 white male twins from the World War II Veteran Twins Registry, Tanner et al. (1999) found similar pairwise PD concordance in 71 monozygotic and 90 dizygotic pairs (0.155 MZ vs 0.111 DZ; relative risk 1.39), concluding that genetic factors do not play a major role in typical PD and that no genetic component is evident when disease begins after age 50 years.
quotes: In 71 MZ and 90 DZ pairs with complete diagnoses, pairwise concordance was similar (0.129 overall, 0.155 MZ, 0.111 DZ; relative risk, 1.39; 95% confidence interval, 0.63-3.1).
The similarity in concordance overall indicates that genetic factors do not play a major role in causing typical PD. No genetic component is evident when the disease begins after age 50 years.

notes.statement: Tanner et al. (1999) found that in 16 twin pairs with diagnosis at or before age 50 years in at least 1 twin, MZ concordance was 1.0 (4 pairs) and DZ concordance was 0.167 (relative risk 6.0), suggesting that genetic factors appear to be important when PD begins at or before age 50 years.
quotes: In 16 pairs with diagnosis at or before age 50 years in at least 1 twin, MZ concordance was 1.0 (4 pairs), and DZ was 0.167 (relative risk, 6.0; 95% confidence interval, 1.69-21.26).
However, genetic factors appear to be important when disease begins at or before age 50 years.

notes.statement: Tanner et al. (1999) estimated a concordance-adjusted PD prevalence of 8.67 per 1,000 among white male World War II veteran twins.
quotes: 193 twins with PD were identified (concordance-adjusted prevalence, 8.67/1000)

notes.statement: Zareparsi et al. (1998) ran complex segregation analyses on the kindreds of 136 PD patients randomly ascertained from a clinic population. They rejected the hypotheses of a nontransmissible environmental factor, of no major gene (sporadic), and of all Mendelian modes of inheritance (dominant, recessive, additive, decreasing) (P less than 0.001).
quotes: we performed complex segregation analyses using kindreds of 136 PD patients randomly ascertained from a clinic population
The hypotheses of a nontransmissible environmental factor, no major gene or type (sporadic), and all Mendelian inheritance (dominant, recessive, additive, decreasing) were rejected (P <0.001).

notes.statement: Zareparsi et al. (1998) concluded that a rare familial factor best explained the familial clustering of PD in their data. This factor was transmitted in a non-Mendelian fashion and influenced age at onset rather than susceptibility. If confirmed, they noted, this would matter for gene-mapping studies that look for Mendelian susceptibility genes.
quotes: Familial clustering of PD in this data set is best explained by a rare familial factor which a) is transmitted in a nonMendelian fashion, and b) influences the age at onset of PD.

notes.statement: Zareparsi et al. (1998) stated that nearly 20% of PD is familial and that only a small subset of familial cases shows autosomal dominant transmission.
quotes: Nearly 20% of PD is familial, a small subset of which exhibits autosomal dominant transmission.

notes.statement: Bordet et al. (1994) used PCR combined with XbaI RFLP analysis to look for CYP2D6 mutations linked to the debrisoquine/sparteine poor-metabolizer phenotype. They tested 105 Caucasian patients with idiopathic Parkinson disease and 15 patients with diffuse Lewy body disease. The rate of genotypically defined poor metabolizers and the frequency of the D6-B mutation did not differ significantly between the two groups. The authors found no relationship between CYP2D6 impairment and how widely neuropathologic lesions spread, but noted that their study could not exclude a role for neuronal expression of CYP2D6.
quotes: We investigated genetic polymorphism of the cytochrome P450 CYP 2D6 gene in 105 caucasian patients with idiopathic Parkinson's disease (IPD) and 15 patients with diffuse Lewy body disease (DLBD).
The rate of genotypically defined PM and the frequencies of the mutation D6-B were not significantly different in IPD and DLBD patients.
This study fails to find a relationship between CYP 2D6 impairment and neuropathological lesions diffusion in IPD and DLBD. This study cannot exclude involvement of neuronal expression of CYP 2D6.

notes.statement: Nussbaum and Polymeropoulos (1997) noted that hereditary influences in PD had been discounted because of a high monozygotic twin discordance rate in studies later shown to be inadequate and inconclusive, and that interest in hereditary factors revived when a positive family history became apparent as a major risk factor.
quotes: Hereditary influences were actually discounted because of a high monozygotic twin discordance rate found in studies that were later shown to be inadequate and inconclusive.
it became more and more apparent that a positive family history was a major risk factor for the disease

notes.statement: Nussbaum and Polymeropoulos (1997) reviewed that the common idiopathic form of PD has a pathologic correlate, Lewy bodies, distributed diffusely throughout the substantia nigra, hypothalamus, hippocampus, autonomic ganglia, and olfactory tracts. They suggested that at least some familial PD with diffuse Lewy bodies results from an abnormal alpha-synuclein protein that interferes with normal protein degradation, leading to inclusions and neuronal death, possibly with mechanisms in common with beta-amyloid and presenilin mutations in Alzheimer disease.
quotes: the existence of Lewy bodies, an eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusion body, distributed diffusely throughout the substantia nigra, hypothalamus, hippocampus, autonomic ganglia and olfactory tracts

suggests that at least some fraction of familial PD with diffuse Lewy bodies is the result of an abnormal protein that interferes with normal protein degradation leading to the development of inclusions and ultimately neuronal cell death

notes.statement: Nussbaum and Polymeropoulos (1997) reviewed that candidate gene linkage approaches in PD families had not been rewarding, but a genomewide scan mapped PD to 4q21-q23 in a large family with PD with diffuse Lewy bodies, a region containing alpha-synuclein, in which a missense mutation was identified in 4 independent PD families.
quotes: a genome wide scan mapped PD to 4q21-23 in one large family with PD with diffuse Lewy bodies, where a candidate gene, alpha-synuclein, resides
The identification of a missense mutation in the alpha-synuclein gene in four independent PD families

notes.statement: Polymeropoulos et al. (1997) described Parkinson disease as a common neurodegenerative disorder with a lifetime incidence of approximately 2%, with a documented pattern of familial aggregation.
quotes: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a common neurodegenerative disorder with a lifetime incidence of approximately 2 percent. A pattern of familial aggregation has been documented for the disorder

notes.statement: Neudorfer et al. (1996) described 6 patients with type I Gaucher disease, which had been considered non-neuronopathic, who developed an atypical parkinsonian syndrome. Signs appeared in the fourth to sixth decade of life, progressed aggressively, and were refractory to conventional anti-Parkinson therapy.
quotes: Type I has hitherto been considered non-neuronopathic. We present six cases and a review of the literature of Parkinsonian symptoms in type I Gaucher disease patients.

The hallmark of this atypical Parkinsonian syndrome is a relatively severe clinical course with early appearance of neurological signs in the 4th to 6th decade of life, aggressive progression of the signs and refractoriness to conventional anti-Parkinson therapy.

notes.statement: Polymeropoulos et al. (1996) found that genetic markers on chromosome 4q21-q23 were linked to Parkinson disease in a large kindred with autosomal dominant PD. The maximum lod score was 6.00 for marker D4S2380.
quotes: Genetic markers on chromosome 4q21-q23 were found to be linked to the PD phenotype in a large kindred with autosomal dominant PD, with a Zmax = 6.00 for marker D4S2380.

notes.statement: Polymeropoulos et al. (1996) noted that Parkinson disease is the second most common neurodegenerative disorder after Alzheimer disease and affects about 1% of the population over age 50. They also noted that recent studies had confirmed significant familial aggregation of PD.
quotes: Parkinson's disease (PD) is the second most common neurodegenerative disorder after Alzheimer's disease, affecting approximately 1 percent of the population over age 50.
Recent studies have confirmed significant familial aggregation of PD and a large number of large multicase families have been documented.

notes.statement: Bandmann et al. (1996) analyzed the H5 pore region of hiGIRK2 (KCNJ7) in familial and sporadic cases of Parkinson disease. Weaver is a mutant mouse strain with dopaminergic cell loss, and KCNJ7 is the human homologue of its causative gene, mGIRK2. The sequence was normal in all cases examined. The authors concluded that nigral cell loss probably has a different cause in Parkinson disease and in weaver mice.
quotes: we analysed the H5 pore region of hiGIRK2 in familial and sporadic cases of Parkinson's disease. The sequence was normal in all cases examined, suggesting a differing aetiology of nigral cell loss in Parkinson's disease and weaver mice.

notes.statement: Bandmann et al. (1996) noted that homozygous weaver mice show progressive postnatal loss of dopaminergic cells in the mesencephalon and had been proposed as an animal model for Parkinson disease. The causative gene, mGIRK2, has a homozygous mutation in the H5 pore region of the channel.
quotes: Homozygous weaver mice, a mutant mouse strain, display progressive postnatal depletion of dopaminergic cells in the mesencephalon and have thus been proposed as an animal model for Parkinson's disease.

notes.statement: In a case-control study of 108 patients with young-onset (age 51 years or younger) Parkinson disease and 236 controls, Sandy et al. (1996) found no significant differences in CYP2D6 allele frequencies. The B allele frequency was slightly lower in patients than in controls (0.14 vs 0.20; p = 0.10). Carrying one or more nonfunctional alleles (A, B, D, and D2) was not associated with increased risk (odds ratio 0.68; 95% CI 0.41 to 1.13).
quotes: compared the distributions of CYP2D6 genotypes between young-onset ( < or = 51 years) PD patients (n = 108) and controls (n = 236)
The frequency of the B allele was slightly lower in the young-onset PD cases than in the controls (0.14 versus 0.20) (X2 = 2.66, p = 0.10).
nor was the presence of one or more nonfunctional alleles (i.e., A, B, D, and D2) (odds ratio 0.68; 95% CI 0.41 to 1.13)

notes.statement: Sandy et al. (1996) suggested that patients with young-onset Parkinson disease may differ from those with older onset in their risk factors. Genotyping studies in older-onset patients had reported modest increases in risk with the CYP2D6 B and A alleles, but the authors found no such association in young-onset patients.
quotes: This study suggests that the young-onset PD population may differ from the older-onset population with respect to risk factors.
Genotyping studies in patients with an older age at onset have reported modest increases in risk associated with the CYP2D6 B and A alleles

notes.statement: Bonifati et al. (1995) found that in 22 multicase PD families, crude segregation ratios were similar for parents and siblings, lifetime cumulative risk approached 0.4 in siblings, and ancestral relatives were all unilaterally distributed; they concluded that autosomal dominant inheritance with strongly age-related penetrance was most likely in familial PD.
quotes: the crude segregation ratios were similar for parents and siblings and the lifetime cumulative risks approached 0.4 in siblings and tended to be comparable, but at later ages, in parents. Ancestral relatives were all unilaterally distributed.
The clinical genetic analyses support autosomal dominant inheritance with strongly age-related penetrance as most likely in familial PD.

notes.statement: Bonifati et al. (1995) found a positive family history for PD in 24% of 100 consecutive PD cases versus 6% of spouse controls; including isolated tremor, the figures were 43% versus 9%.
quotes: Family history for PD was positive in 24% of consecutive PD cases and in 6% of spouse controls (p < 0.001). When family history for isolated tremor is also considered, the number of positive cases rises to 43% compared with 9% in controls (p < 0.001).

notes.statement: Bonifati et al. (1995) found that familial PD cases had an earlier age at onset than sporadic cases from the same consecutive series, and that familial and sporadic PD differed only in onset age.
quotes: These familial cases showed an earlier onset age when compared with sporadic ones from the same consecutive series.
Familial and sporadic PD only differ in onset age.

notes.statement: Planté-Bordeneuve et al. (1995) compared 31 patients with familial PD from 14 families with 31 age-matched patients with sporadic PD and found no statistical difference in selected clinical parameters. In familial cases, clinical parameters and disease course varied within and between families.
quotes: This group was compared for selected clinical parameters to 31 age matched patients with sporadic PD. No statistical difference was found between the two groups.
In familial cases, both the clinical parameters studied and the course of the disease varied within and between families, as observed in sporadic cases.

notes.statement: Planté-Bordeneuve et al. (1995) found that transmission in 14 PD families was compatible with autosomal dominant inheritance. A total segregation ratio of 0.25 suggested incomplete penetrance, which increased with age from 0 below age 30 to 0.43 over age 70.
quotes: The genetic transmission was compatible with an autosomal dominant model.
The total segregation ratio of 0.25 suggested an incomplete penetrance, which increased with age, from 0 below the age of 30 to 0.43 over the age of 70.

notes.statement: In 8 multigeneration kindreds, Planté-Bordeneuve et al. (1995) found that age at onset was earlier in children than in their parents (mean difference 26 years), whereas it was similar within a generation. Although an ascertainment bias could not be excluded, the authors suggested the results were compatible with anticipation.
quotes: Age at onset was earlier in children than in their parents in the 8 multigeneration kindreds studied (mean difference 26 +/- 4.6 years, p = 0.01), whereas it was identical within a generation (mean difference 4.7 +/- 5.7 years, p = 0.1).
Although we cannot exclude an ascertainment bias, our results are compatible with an anticipation phenomenon, which deserves further studies for confirmation.

notes.statement: Sommer and Rocca (1996) discussed prion analogues and twin studies in Parkinson disease.
quotes: Prion analogues and twin studies in Parkinson's disease.

notes.statement: Kurth et al. (1993) identified a single-stranded conformational polymorphism in a Hae III-digested MAOB PCR product. Allele 1 frequency was 0.62 in 46 PD patients versus 0.45 in 121 controls, and allele 1 was associated with a relative risk for PD of 2.03 (p < 0.02). The authors suggested that an inherited variant of MAOB may be involved in a genetic predisposition to PD.
quotes: One hundred twenty-one control individuals were allelotyped with frequencies of 0.45 and 0.55 for alleles 1 and 2, respectively.
The presence of MAO-B allele 1 is associated with a relative risk for PD of 2.03-fold (confidence interval, 1.44-2.61; p < 0.02).
These results suggest that an inherited variant of MAO-B may be involved in a genetic predisposition for PD.

notes.statement: Kurth et al. (1993) found no statistically significant differences in allele frequencies for an MAOA polymorphism between the same PD patients and controls.
quotes: For comparison, a monoamine oxidase A polymorphism was used to determine allelic frequencies in these same populations and no statistically significant differences were found.

notes.statement: Lazzarini et al. (1994) used survival analysis on first-degree relatives of consecutively seen PD probands. Siblings of probands who had an affected parent had a significantly higher cumulative risk than siblings of probands without an affected parent. The authors took this to suggest significant familial aggregation in a subset of randomly ascertained families.
quotes: When we considered siblings of probands with affected parents, the cumulative risk increased significantly over siblings of probands without affected parents, suggesting significant familial aggregation in a subset of randomly ascertained families.

notes.statement: Lazzarini et al. (1994) analyzed 80 multicase families and found age-adjusted segregation ratios approaching 0.5. Affected parents and affected siblings occurred in similar proportions. These findings, together with the distribution of ancestral secondary cases, were compatible with autosomal dominant inheritance with reduced penetrance in a subset of PD.
quotes: Age-adjusted segregation ratios approaching 0.5 and similar proportions of affected parents and siblings, as well as the distribution of ancestral secondary cases, were compatible with an autosomal dominant mode of inheritance with reduced penetrance in a subset of PD.

notes.statement: Payami et al. (1995) studied age at onset and family history in 137 probands with idiopathic PD. Probands with an affected parent, aunt, or uncle had a significantly earlier onset (47.7 years) than those with an affected sib only (60.3 years) or with no affected relatives (59.2 years).
quotes: We studied age at onset and family history of 137 patients (probands) with the diagnosis of idiopathic Parkinson's disease (PD).
Probands (N = 21) who had an affected parent, aunt, or uncle were younger (p = 0.0001) at the onset of PD (47.7 +/- 8.8 years)

notes.statement: Payami et al. (1995) found that onset was earlier in the proband generation than in the parental generation, by an average of 17 years. Within families, the calendar years of onset varied too much to suggest a common point of exposure. The authors concluded that their data were most compatible with genetic anticipation, which could suggest involvement of an unstable trinucleotide repeat.
quotes: Age at onset was earlier, by an average of 17 years, in the proband generation than in the parental generation.
The intrafamily variation in the calendar year of onset was too great to suggest a common point of exposure.
Our data are most compatible with genetic anticipation, which could suggest involvement of an unstable trinucleotide repeat.

notes.statement: Ho et al. (1995) identified a single-stranded conformational polymorphism (A or G) in the monoamine oxidase B gene, 36 bases upstream from the intron 13-exon 14 boundary. In an allelic association study, they found no statistically significant association between this polymorphism and Parkinson disease, contrary to the results of a previous study.
quotes: A single-stranded conformational polymorphism in the monoamine oxidase B gene was shown to be A or G, 36 bases upstream from the intron 13-exon 14 boundary.
An allelic association study revealed no statistically significant associations between this single-base polymorphism and Parkinson's disease, unlike the results of a previous study.

notes.statement: Markopoulou et al. (1995) observed anticipation in a Greek-American kindred with autosomal dominant levodopa-responsive parkinsonism: affected members of the third generation had onset at ages 50 to 71, those of the fourth at 40 to 55, and the one in the fifth at age 31 years.
quotes: Anticipation is present in this pedigree. The affected members in the third generation developed symptoms at ages 50 to 71, in the fourth at ages 40 to 55, and in the fifth at age 31 years.

notes.statement: Markopoulou et al. (1995) argued that the inheritance pattern and the occurrence of parkinsonism in successive generations living on two continents (Greece and the United States) challenged environmental factors as the primary cause of parkinsonism in this kindred.
quotes: The inheritance pattern and the development of parkinsonism in successive generations on two continents challenges environmental factors as the primary cause in the pathogenesis of parkinsonism in this kindred.

notes.statement: In a door-to-door survey of 982 people older than 65 years in two rural Bavarian villages, Trenkwalder et al. (1995) found a prevalence of Parkinson disease of 0.71% (95% CI, 0.19-1.23%). More men than women were affected (5 men, 2 women).
quotes: We investigated the prevalence of PS in a rural Bavarian population of individuals older than 65 years (982 participants; response rate, 82.5%) using a door-to-door-survey and a biphasic approach.
The prevalence of Parkinson's disease in individuals older than 65 years was 0.71% (95% confidence interval, 0.19% to 1.23%), with a male predominance (five men, two women).

notes.statement: Trenkwalder et al. (1995) found other causes of parkinsonism in the same population: drug-induced parkinsonism (0.41%), vascular parkinsonism (0.20%), multiple system atrophy (0.31%), Fahr disease (0.10%), and normal-pressure hydrocephalus (0.41%). Fifty percent of parkinsonism cases had not been diagnosed before the survey.
quotes: Parkinsonism of other pathogenesis included drug-induced PS (0.41%, four of 982 inhabitants), vascular PS (0.20%, two of 982), multiple system atrophy (0.31%, three of 982), and Fahr's disease (0.10%, one of 982).
Fifty percent of cases of PS were newly diagnosed.

notes.statement: Parboosingh et al. (1995) used single-strand conformation analysis to screen the Cu/Zn superoxide dismutase, Mn superoxide dismutase and catalase genes in 107 unrelated patients with familial or sporadic PD. They found no mutations and concluded that PD is not caused by mutations in these 3 detoxifying enzyme genes.
quotes: A total of 107 unrelated patients with PD from two PD populations (familial and sporadic) were screened for mutations in the genes of copper/zinc superoxide dismutase, manganese superoxide dismutase, and catalase by single-strand conformation analysis.
Parkinson's disease is not caused by mutations in the genes of these three detoxifying enzymes.

notes.statement: Duvoisin et al. (1981) found zero concordance for Parkinson disease in the first 12 monozygotic twin pairs examined in an ongoing twin study. They concluded that these preliminary findings suggested that genetic factors do not play a major role in the etiology of Parkinson disease.
quotes: Zero concordance for Parkinson disease was found in the first 12 monozygotic twin pairs examined in an ongoing twin study.
These preliminary findings suggest that genetic factors do not play a major role in the etiology of Parkinson disease

notes.statement: Duvoisin et al. (1981) found that cigarette smoking appeared less frequent in probands with PD than in their unaffected monozygotic co-twins (11.9 vs 16.1 pack-years). They also found evidence of premorbid personality differences dating back to late adolescence or early adult years, which they took to point to a prodromal onset of the disease that early.
quotes: Cigarette smoking appeared to be less frequent in the probands than in the co-twins (11.9 versus 16.1 pack-years).
There was also evidence of premorbid personality differences between probands and co-twins dating back to late adolescence or early adult years.
