point to a prodromal onset of the disease as early as late adolescence or early adult life

notes.statement: Barbeau and Pourcher (1982) found familial cases in 46% of patients whose parkinsonism began before age 40. This was higher than the 10 to 15% seen in general Parkinson disease populations.
quotes: In this early onset group of patients, there was a 46% incidence of familial cases (as opposed to 10-15% in the general Parkinson populations).

notes.statement: Barbeau and Pourcher (1982) found a high prevalence of essential tremor in the families of patients with tremor-onset early parkinsonism. In the families of patients with akineto-rigid onset, other cases of Parkinson disease were frequent. Familial grey hair, hypertension, diabetes and thyroid disease appeared more often than expected.
quotes: The cases with tremor onset had a high prevalence of essential tremor in their families, while those with an akineto-rigid onset had a high familial incidence of other cases of Parkinson's Disease.
Familial grey hair, hypertension, diabetes and thyroidopathies appeared to be in higher than expected frequency.

notes.statement: Langston et al. (1983) described 4 persons who developed marked parkinsonism after intravenous use of an illicit drug; analysis of the substance injected by 2 of them showed mainly 1-methyl-4-phenyl-1,2,5,6-tetrahydropyridine (MPTP) with trace amounts of the meperidine analog MPPP. Based on the parkinsonian features and pathologic data from a previously reported case, they proposed that MPTP selectively damages cells in the substantia nigra.
quotes: Four persons developed marked parkinsonism after using an illicit drug intravenously. Analysis of the substance injected by two of these patients revealed primarily 1-methyl-4-phenyl-1,2,5,6-tetrahydropyridine (MPTP) with trace amounts of 1-methyl-4-phenyl-4-propionoxy-piperidine (MPPP).
it is proposed that this chemical selectively damages cells in the substantia nigra.

notes.statement: Ward et al. (1983) studied 43 monozygotic (MZ) and 19 dizygotic (DZ) twin pairs in which an index case had definite Parkinson disease and found only one MZ pair definitely concordant. When pairs with questionable clinical features were included, 4 of 48 MZ and 1 of 19 DZ pairs were concordant.
quotes: Among 43 monozygotic (MZ) and 19 dizygotic (DZ) pairs in which an index case had definite Parkinson's disease (PD), only one MZ pair was definitely concordant for PD.
When pairs with questionable clinical features were included, 4 of 48 MZ and 1 of 19 DZ pairs were concordant.

notes.statement: Ward et al. (1983) found that the frequency of PD in MZ cotwins of index cases was similar to that expected in an age- and sex-matched unrelated control group. Although they could not identify a single environmental agent, they concluded that the major factors in the etiology of PD are nongenetic.
quotes: The frequency of PD in MZ cotwins of index cases with PD was similar to that expected in an unrelated control group matched for age and sex.
Although we were unable to identify a single environmental agent, we conclude that the major factors in the etiology of PD are nongenetic.

notes.statement: Calne and Langston (1983) suggested that in most cases of Parkinson disease the cause may be an environmental factor, possibly toxic, superimposed on a background of slow, sustained neuronal loss due to advancing age.
quotes: It is suggested here that in most cases of Parkinson's disease the cause may be an environmental factor, possibly toxic, superimposed on a background of slow, sustained neuronal loss due to advancing age.

notes.statement: Kondo et al. (1973) carried out a genetic analysis of Parkinson disease and reported evidence of a multifactorial etiology.
quotes: Parkinson's disease. Genetic analysis and evidence of a multifactorial etiology.

notes.statement: Duvoisin (1987) reviewed the genetics of Parkinson disease and concluded that the best available data did not support a role of heredity in its etiology. Case-control studies had failed to show a prevalence of PD among first-degree relatives of index cases significantly higher than in controls, and concordance in monozygotic twins was unexpectedly low and not significantly different from that in dizygotic twins. He noted, however, that a nonhereditary, possibly congenital genetic defect was not excluded.
quotes: Case control studies have failed to document a prevalence of PD among first-degree relatives of index cases significantly exceeding that found in control groups.

the concordance rate for PD among monozygotic twins has been found to be unexpectedly low and not significantly different from that among dizygotic twins or the prevalence among first-degree relatives.
Thus, the best available data do not support a role of heredity in the etiology of PD. A nonhereditary, possibly congenital genetic defect is, however, not excluded.

notes.statement: Duvoisin (1987) noted that the idea of a hereditary role in PD arose from positive family histories, reports of kindreds with parkinsonism, and the first systematic family study by Mjones. He argued that closer study of the clinical data showed these familial clusters of parkinsonism reflected other disorders, notably olivopontocerebellar atrophy (OPCA) and other forms of multiple system atrophy.
quotes: It was reinforced by the first systematic family study of PD conducted a half-century ago by Mjones.
However, closer study of the clinical data indicates that familial aggregations of parkinsonism have reflected various other disorders, notably OPCA and other forms of multiple system atrophy.

notes.statement: In a hospital-based survey of age-specific prevalence of Parkinson disease among 551 patients from Helsinki and Vancouver, Teräväinen et al. (1986) concluded that the disorder may be starting earlier than it did previously. They discussed what this finding might mean for the etiology of Parkinson disease.
quotes: We have conducted a hospital-based survey of the age-specific prevalence of Parkinson's disease in 551 patients from Helsinki and Vancouver.
We conclude that the disorder may be starting earlier than previously and we discuss the implications of this finding for the etiology of Parkinson's disease.

notes.statement: Calne et al. (1987) reported 6 families with Parkinson disease in which symptoms tended to begin at about the same calendar time regardless of the patient's age. The mean difference in time of onset between generations was 4.6 years, while the mean difference in age at onset between children and parents was 25.2 years. The authors took this as suggestive of an environmental rather than a genetic cause, supported by the lack of correlation between occurrence of the disease and degree of consanguinity.
quotes: The mean difference in the time of onset in different generations was 4.6 years while the mean difference in age of onset in children and parents was 25.2 years.

We construe this pattern of age separation within families as suggestive of an environmental rather than genetic cause. Support for this view derives from the lack of correlation between occurrence of the disease and the degree of consanguinity.

notes.statement: Calne et al. (1987) concluded that their findings fit the hypothesis that some cases of Parkinson disease are caused by early, subclinical environmental damage followed by age-related loss of neurons in the central nervous system.
quotes: We conclude that our findings are in accord with the hypothesis which attributes the cause of some cases of Parkinson's disease to early, subclinical environmental damage followed by age-related attrition of neurons within the central nervous system.

notes.statement: Barbeau et al. (1985) postulated that Parkinson disease results from environmental factors acting on genetically susceptible individuals against a background of normal aging, and noted that many potentially neurotoxic xenobiotics are detoxified by hepatic cytochrome P450.
quotes: It is postulated that Parkinson's disease is the result of environmental factors acting on genetically susceptible individuals against a background of normal ageing.
Many potentially neurotoxic xenobiotics are detoxified by hepatic cytochrome P450.

notes.statement: Barbeau et al. (1985) studied debrisoquine 4-hydroxylation in 40 patients with Parkinson disease and 40 normal controls and found that significantly more parkinsonian patients than controls had partially or totally defective 4-hydroxylation. Poor metabolizers of debrisoquine tended to have had earlier onset of disease.
quotes: Significantly more parkinsonian than control subjects had partially or totally defective 4-hydroxylation of debrisoquine.
Poor metabolisers of debrisoquine tended to have had earlier onset of disease.

notes.statement: Di Monte (1991) reviewed evidence that impaired mitochondrial function may underlie neuronal death in Parkinson disease: MPP+, the toxic metabolite of MPTP, likely blocks mitochondrial electron flow at complex I, and complex I activity is deficient in brain and other tissues of parkinsonian patients. Because 7 complex I subunit genes are encoded by mtDNA, Di Monte (1991) suggested that abnormal mtDNA might play a role in PD pathogenesis.
quotes: the toxicity of MPP+ is likely to result from its ability to block mitochondrial electron flow at the level of complex I
recent studies have revealed a deficiency of mitochondrial complex I activity in the brain as well as other tissues of parkinsonian patients
Since seven of these genes are localized in the mitochondrial genome, it is conceivable that abnormal mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) might play a role in the pathogenesis of Parkinson's disease.

notes.statement: Hughes et al. (1992) examined the brains of 100 patients whom consultant neurologists had diagnosed prospectively as having idiopathic Parkinson disease. Only 76 had nigral Lewy bodies. The other 24 had diagnoses that included progressive supranuclear palsy, multiple system atrophy, Alzheimer disease, Alzheimer-type pathology and basal ganglia vascular disease.
quotes: The pathological findings in 100 patients diagnosed prospectively by a group of consultant neurologists as having idiopathic Parkinson's disease are reported.
In 24 cases without Lewy bodies, diagnoses included progressive supranuclear palsy, multiple system atrophy, Alzheimer's disease, Alzheimer-type pathology, and basal ganglia vascular disease.

notes.statement: Hughes et al. (1992) found that applying the recommended diagnostic criteria retrospectively raised clinical diagnostic accuracy to 82%. The authors concluded that their observations called into question the concept of Parkinson disease as a single distinct morbid entity.
quotes: The retrospective application of recommended diagnostic criteria improved the diagnostic accuracy to 82%.
These observations call into question current concepts of Parkinson's disease as a single distinct morbid entity.

notes.statement: Hughes et al. (1992) found Lewy bodies in the cerebral cortex of every one of the 76 patients with nigral Lewy bodies whose clinical diagnosis had been idiopathic Parkinson disease.
quotes: Seventy six had nigral Lewy bodies, and in all of these Lewy bodies were also found in the cerebral cortex.

notes.statement: Kissel and Andre (1976) suggested that a genetically determined anomaly of dopamine metabolism was probably responsible for the association of Parkinson disease and anosmia, noting that two families with the same association had been reported previously.
quotes: Two families with the same association had been previously reported. An anomaly of the metabolism of dopamine, genetically determined, is probably responsible for these disorders.

notes.statement: Young et al. (1977) studied affected ancestral second-degree relatives in 12 Parkinson disease families. Affected relatives were found on both sides of the family more often than expected for autosomal dominant inheritance. The authors concluded that most cases of Parkinson disease have a multifactorial cause, although dominant inheritance in some families was not entirely ruled out.
